captions.text: They use the modern to protect the traditional.
That is a fascinating counterpoint and it really changes
how you read the ending.
It's not just good versus evil.
It's the empire aggressively regulating its borders.
So to reframe the entire novel for you, Count
Dracula was never felled by religious piety or sheer
brute strength alone. Yes.
They used crucifixes and yes, they used a Bowie
knife at the very end.
But those were just the finishing tools.
They weren't the strategy.
The strategy was data.
The vampire was audited, tracked, and dismantled by the
unstoppable paper trail and communication networks of
the modern bureaucratic state.
The true stake through the heart of the vampire
was the shipping manifest, the train timetable,
and the typewritten chronological database.
Once again, it was the filing cabinet that slays
the monster. The archaic warlord was completely
dismantled by the administrative clerk, which leaves us
